issues.observed: In the closed FCSTM, transition:line:22 (DoorOpenWithItem->DoorShutWithItem, trigger Door_Closed) and transition:line:23 (DoorOpenWithItem->ReadytoCook, trigger Cooking_Time_Entered) both have guard=null; no guard expression exists anywhere in the model (guarded_transition_count=0 per inspection metrics), so the 'zero time set' qualifier on the door-closed alternative is entirely unmodeled and the two alternatives are distinguished only by differing trigger events (Door_Closed vs Cooking_Time_Entered) rather than by the required guard partition over cooking time.
issues.reason: The NL explicitly attaches a guard-like qualifier ('with zero time set') to only one of two same-source alternatives while the other lacks a directly opposing complementary guard; per the guard_disjointness cross-frontier discipline, this compares the group's guard relation together rather than each endpoint individually, and the closed model implements neither guard, exposing an unresolved and unmodeled distinguishing condition on the cooking-time variable that must be preserved as an explicit possible violation rather than silently discharged by the endpoint/trigger-only match.
issues.requirement_quote: the system can transition to DoorShutWithItem if the door is closed with zero time set or to ReadytoCook if cooking time is entered
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The two alternatives already use distinct events (Door_Closed vs Cooking_Time_Entered) rather than a shared event with competing guards, so they may already be operationally distinguishable by event alone, and the NL guard clauses may be read as descriptive context of each event's circumstances rather than independently enforced guard predicates; if the grammar attaches 'zero time set' as a scenario qualifier rather than a hard guard, the missing guard may not be a defect.
issues.title: DoorOpenWithItem alternatives to DoorShutWithItem and ReadytoCook carry no modeled guard to distinguish 'zero time set' from 'cooking time entered'

branches.reason: Cross-view comparison of the 25 NL contracts against the exact closed-model transition inventory (16 transitions) and event-consumer facts shows all direct endpoint, retention, and initial-entry obligations are satisfied by exactly-matching edges. The DoorShut initial pseudostate edge (transition:line:16) targets state:DoorShut:line:10, matching NL-CONTRACT-NL1-INITIAL-1's owner=Microwave/target=DoorShut. All transition_endpoints contracts (NL1-3, NL2-4/5, NL3-6/7, NL4-8/9, NL5-11/12, NL6-14/16, NL7-17, NL8-19/20/21) map one-to-one onto exact transitions in the FCSTM inventory with matching source/target/trigger. The retention self-loop DoorShut->DoorShut on Cancel (transition:line:17) satisfies NL1-RETENTION-1. The two event-consumer-coverage derived contracts (door opened in DoorShut, Start in ReadytoCook) are satisfied: Door_Opened is a reachable consumer at DoorShut (transition:line:18) and Start is a reachable consumer at ReadytoCook (transition:line:28), both included in inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers with matching reachable_consumer_transition_refs.
